chapter: Guitar, John Collins and Ellington on the radio
title: The teenage singing trio with Eddie Johnson and Leroy Winbush
summary: Details on his trio with Leroy Winbush and Eddie Johnson, performing at Doc Huggins' club where John Collins played.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Who was the other member of the trio besides you and Eddie?

His name was Leroy Winbush (MONROE). Oh, I guess he's got his first dollar. He's very wealthy today. He went into commercial art, like E. Simmons [Easoms] Campbell, and he has all the accounts, the banks and things in the Loop in Chicago.
Was [Easoms] Campbell from Chicago?
No, not [Easoms] Campbell. What I was speaking of --
That kind of artwork?
That kind of work.
I see. Yes.

And Eddie told me a thing that -- when he was here -- that he had a thing to go to Singapore with the Chinese government, and Roy was always smart in that direction, you know. Even when he was about 17 and we were together, you know? And he made quite a success of himself, and he's got a good business head, and straight ahead, and his feet are still on the ground. In fact, Eddie was trying to get me to get a picture of us, because Roy wanted it, to use it for a TV show that they might make a special, on him. You know? Because
he's a quiet man.
Do you still have the picture?

Couldn't find it. Looked for it and couldn't find it. Now, I have another one, but I think Roy wanted the one that -- I know the one that Roy wanted. Oh, let's see, we were about -- Roy was 17, I was 15 and Eddie was 13. And we were just kids, you know?
Uh-huh. How long did you keep the trio together?
Oh, let me see. Quite a few years. Oh, maybe three or four. That was a long time to us in those days, you know?
Sure. Well, to teenagers it is.
Yeah. And we didn't quite realize what we had at that time. We just were doing like a neighborhood thing, you know, having a good time and playing at little parties.
What was the name of the club that John was working in?
Oh, John Collins.
Yeah, uh-huh. When you said that --
Doc Huggins'.
Uh-huh.
And this same trio came in, we came in to perform, and you know, because as I was saying we made a little
noise and John Collins was playing there with his mother, you know, as I said before.
Uh-huh.
And Dan Grissom. All three of us in the trio played guitar, but I turned out to be a chief guitar player, if you want to put it that way.
(Laughter)
And he said, 'Well, now, Jim, you play guitar and pass out the singing notes.' So I would rehearse everybody. But I was the only one that sang out of tune.
(Laughter)
Everybody else could sing, you know. Roy was a little slow on getting his part, but when he got it you couldn't move him.
